section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of conic sections (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) as slices of a cone. State the central challenge: How do we prove that a flat slice of a cone perfectly matches the algebraic definition of these curves?
section_1.example: Imagine a chef precisely slicing a solid chocolate cone with a flat knife. Depending on the angle, the rim of the chocolate slice changes shape. We need to find the 'focal points' of that chocolate slice.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem
section_2.content: Review the 'Tangent Segments Theorem': Two tangent segments to a sphere from the same external point are equal in length. This is the foundational logic for the Dandelin proof.
section_2.example: Visualize a basketball sitting in a hoop (a ring). Any point on that ring is the same distance to the point where the ball touches the ground if it were dropped vertically.

section_3.title: Enter the Dandelin Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce Germinal Dandelin's brilliant 1822 insight. For an elliptical slice, place two spheres inside the cone: one above the plane and one below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the cutting plane at exactly one point.
section_3.example: Imagine inflating two balloons inside a glass cone until they are wedged tight against the walls and just barely 'kiss' the slanted glass shelf (the cutting plane) passing through the middle.

section_4.title: Defining the Foci
section_4.content: Explain that the two points where the spheres touch the plane (F1 and F2) are exactly the foci of the ellipse. Pick an arbitrary point 'P' on the edge of the slice (the curve).
section_4.example: A tiny ant (Point P) walks along the edge of the cut. We are going to track the distance from the ant to the two 'kissing points' (F1 and F2) of the balloons.

section_5.title: The Visual Proof (The String Property)
section_5.content: Show that the distance PF1 equals the segment on the cone's surface from P to the top sphere's contact circle. Similarly for PF2 and the bottom sphere. Because these segments lie on the same 'generator line' of the cone, their sum (PF1 + PF2) is always equal to the fixed distance between the two circles of tangency.
section_5.example: Animate a string connecting F1 to the ant (P) and then to F2. As the ant moves, the string length remains constant, visually demonstrating the definition of an ellipse: PF1 + PF2 = Constant.

section_6.title: Universal Application
section_6.content: Briefly demonstrate that this logic isn't just for ellipses. By changing the angle of the plane, Dandelin spheres can also define the focus of a parabola or the two foci of a hyperbola.
section_6.example: Tilt the glass shelf steeply. One balloon moves to the other side of the cone's vertex. The 'sum' of distances becomes a 'difference,' perfectly matching the geometric definition of a hyperbola.

section_7.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
section_7.content: Summarize how Dandelin spheres bridge the gap between 3D solid geometry and 2D coordinate geometry. Mention how this explains planetary orbits and satellite dish designs.
section_7.example: Think of a satellite dish: its parabolic shape is designed so all 'rays' hit a single focus, just like the point where a single Dandelin sphere would touch that parabolic slice.

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of conic sections (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) as slices of a cone. State the central challenge: How do we prove that a flat slice of a cone perfectly matches the algebraic definition of these curves?
section_1.example: Imagine a chef precisely slicing a solid chocolate cone with a flat knife. Depending on the angle, the rim of the chocolate slice changes shape. We need to find the 'focal points' of that chocolate slice.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem
section_2.content: Review the 'Tangent Segments Theorem': Two tangent segments to a sphere from the same external point are equal in length. This is the foundational logic for the Dandelin proof.
section_2.example: Visualize a basketball sitting in a hoop (a ring). Any point on that ring is the same distance to the point where the ball touches the ground if it were dropped vertically.

section_3.title: Enter the Dandelin Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce Germinal Dandelin's brilliant 1822 insight. For an elliptical slice, place two spheres inside the cone: one above the plane and one below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the cutting plane at exactly one point.
section_3.example: Imagine inflating two balloons inside a glass cone until they are wedged tight against the walls and just barely 'kiss' the slanted glass shelf (the cutting plane) passing through the middle.

section_4.title: Defining the Foci
section_4.content: Explain that the two points where the spheres touch the plane (F1 and F2) are exactly the foci of the ellipse. Pick an arbitrary point 'P' on the edge of the slice (the curve).
section_4.example: A tiny ant (Point P) walks along the edge of the cut. We are going to track the distance from the ant to the two 'kissing points' (F1 and F2) of the balloons.

section_5.title: The Visual Proof (The String Property)
section_5.content: Show that the distance PF1 equals the segment on the cone's surface from P to the top sphere's contact circle. Similarly for PF2 and the bottom sphere. Because these segments lie on the same 'generator line' of the cone, their sum (PF1 + PF2) is always equal to the fixed distance between the two circles of tangency.
section_5.example: Animate a string connecting F1 to the ant (P) and then to F2. As the ant moves, the string length remains constant, visually demonstrating the definition of an ellipse: PF1 + PF2 = Constant.

section_6.title: Universal Application
section_6.content: Briefly demonstrate that this logic isn't just for ellipses. By changing the angle of the plane, Dandelin spheres can also define the focus of a parabola or the two foci of a hyperbola.
section_6.example: Tilt the glass shelf steeply. One balloon moves to the other side of the cone's vertex. The 'sum' of distances becomes a 'difference,' perfectly matching the geometric definition of a hyperbola.

section_7.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
section_7.content: Summarize how Dandelin spheres bridge the gap between 3D solid geometry and 2D coordinate geometry. Mention how this explains planetary orbits and satellite dish designs.
section_7.example: Think of a satellite dish: its parabolic shape is designed so all 'rays' hit a single focus, just like the point where a single Dandelin sphere would touch that parabolic slice.

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
lecture_lines: Conic sections are formed by slicing a double cone.
We get ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas from different angles.
How do these shapes connect to their algebraic definitions?
animations: Show a 3D cone (#C0C0C0) being intersected by a slanted cutting plane (#00FFFF).
Highlight the intersection curve (ellipse) in #FFD700 as the plane passes through.
Add labels: 'Cone' for the solid and 'Conic Section' for the resulting curve.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem
lecture_lines: Imagine two lines tangent to a sphere from one point.
These two tangent segments are always equal in length.
This simple geometric fact is our most powerful tool.
animations: Display a sphere (#FFFFFF) and a point P (#FF4500) outside of it.
Draw two tangent segments from P to points A and B (#00FF00) on the sphere's surface.
Highlight segments PA and PB, and display the equation 'PA = PB' to show equality.

section_3.title: Enter the Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Place two spheres inside the cone for an ellipse.
Each sphere touches the cone along a perfect circle.
The spheres also touch the cutting plane at one point.
Germinal Dandelin introduced these 'kissing spheres' in 1822.
These spheres reveal the hidden geometry of the conic slice.
animations: Show a translucent cone (#C0C0C0) with a slanted cutting plane (#00FFFF) inside.
Insert a small sphere (#FF69B4) inside the cone, touching both the cone and the plane.
Insert a larger sphere (#1E90FF) below the plane, also touching both the cone and the plane.
Highlight the two circles (#ADFF2F) where the spheres are tangent to the cone's interior wall.
Mark the two 'focal' points (#FFA500) where the spheres touch the cutting plane.

section_4.title: Defining the Foci
lecture_lines: The spheres' contact points on the plane are the foci.
Let's pick any point P on the ellipse's edge.
We will track the distance from P to each focus.
animations: Focus on the cutting plane, labeling the two contact points as F1 and F2 (#FFA500).
Place an arbitrary point P (#FF4500) on the perimeter of the elliptical intersection.
Draw segments from P to F1 and P to F2, highlighting the distance.
Trace a generator line (#FFFFFF) from the cone's vertex through point P.
Identify points T1 and T2 where the generator line meets the two contact circles.

section_5.title: The Visual Proof (The String Property)
lecture_lines: Segment PF1 equals the distance to the top circle.
Segment PF2 equals the distance to the bottom circle.
Both distances lie along the same line on the cone.
Their sum is the fixed distance between the two circles.
This sum remains constant, proving it is an ellipse.
animations: Highlight segments PF1 and PT1, demonstrating they are equal tangents to the top sphere.
Highlight segments PF2 and PT2, demonstrating they are equal tangents to the bottom sphere.
Show that PF1 + PF2 is equal to the length of segment T1T2 on the generator line.
Move point P around the ellipse, showing T1T2 length remains fixed between the circles.
Fade in the defining property: 'PF1 + PF2 = Constant' in #FFD700.

section_6.title: Universal Application
lecture_lines: This logic applies to more than just ellipses.
Tilt the plane to see a parabola's single focus.
Steeper tilts create the two branches of a hyperbola.
One sphere moves above the vertex for the hyperbola.
Dandelin spheres unify all conics through one geometric proof.
animations: Tilt the cutting plane (#00FFFF) to demonstrate the formation of a parabola.
Adjust the plane to a steeper angle to show the two branches of a hyperbola.
Show Dandelin spheres for these cases, touching the plane at the new focal points.

section_7.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
lecture_lines: Dandelin's spheres bridge 3D shapes and 2D curves.
This geometry explains orbits, reflectors, and satellite dishes.
Pure geometry reveals the deep soul of conic sections.
animations: Transition from the 3D cone/spheres model to a clean 2D elliptical diagram.
Visualize a parabolic satellite dish reflecting parallel rays to a single focal point (#FFFF00).
Display the final summary text: 'Geometry and Algebra Unified' in #00FA9A.

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem"
        lines = [
            "Imagine two lines tangent to a sphere from one point.",
            "These two tangent segments are always equal in length.",
            "This simple geometric fact is our most powerful tool."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a sphere (#FFFFFF) and a point P (#FF4500) outside of it.
        # Sphere represented as a Circle with an Ellipse inside to give 3D depth
        sphere_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        sphere_ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=1.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=1).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        sphere = VGroup(sphere_circle, sphere_ellipse)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        point_p = Dot(color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(point_p, 'C1')
        label_p = MathTex("P", color="#FF4500", font_size=24).next_to(point_p, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw two tangent segments from P to points A and B (#00FF00) on the sphere's surface.
        # We'll calculate tangent points on the circle.
        # Circle center is at self.grid['B2'] to 'E5' center.
        circle_center = sphere.get_center()
        radius = 1.5
        p_pos = point_p.get_center()
        
        # Geometry for tangent points from P to Circle
        # Distance from center to P
        dist = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - circle_center)
        # Angle from center to P
        angle_p = np.arctan2(p_pos[1] - circle_center[1], p_pos[0] - circle_center[0])
        # Angle of tangent points relative to center-P line
        # cos(alpha) = radius / dist
        alpha = np.arccos(radius / dist)
        
        pos_a = circle_center + np.array([
            radius * np.cos(angle_p + alpha),
            radius * np.sin(angle_p + alpha),
            0
        ])
        pos_b = circle_center + np.array([
            radius * np.cos(angle_p - alpha),
            radius * np.sin(angle_p - alpha),
            0
        ])
        
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color="#00FF00")
        dot_b = Dot(pos_b, color="#00FF00")
        label_a = MathTex("A", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(dot_b, DOWN + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color="#00FF00")
        line_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color="#00FF00")
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(line_pa), 
            Create(line_pb), 
            FadeIn(dot_a), 
            FadeIn(dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight segments PA and PB, and display the equation 'PA = PB' to show equality.
        equation = MathTex("PA = PB", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'A4')
        
        # Highlight: briefly pulse the lines
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            line_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            line_pb.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            Write(equation)
        )
        self.play(
            line_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=2),
            line_pb.animate.set_stroke(width=2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Summary & Real-World Connection"
        lines = [
            "Dandelin's spheres bridge 3D shapes and 2D curves.",
            "This geometry explains orbits, reflectors, and satellite dishes.",
            "Pure geometry reveals the deep soul of conic sections."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CONE = "#87CEEB" # Sky Blue
        COLOR_SPHERE = "#FFA07A" # Light Salmon
        COLOR_ELLIPSE = "#F0E68C" # Khaki
        COLOR_RAY = "#FFFF00" # Yellow

        foci = VGroup(
            Dot(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT*0.4, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, radius=0.04),
            Dot(ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT*0.4, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, radius=0.04)
        )
        two_d_model = VGroup(ellipse, foci)
        self.place_in_area(two_d_model, "B4", "C6")

        bridge_arrow = Arrow(three_d_model.get_right(), two_d_model.get_left(), color=WHITE)

        self.play(Create(three_d_model))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(bridge_arrow))
        self.play(Create(two_d_model))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_RAY),
            FadeOut(three_d_model),
            FadeOut(two_d_model),
            FadeOut(bridge_arrow)
        )

        # Parabolic Dish
        dish = ArcBetweenPoints(
            self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5, 
            self.grid["E5"] + RIGHT*0.5, 
            angle=-TAU/4, 
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        # Focal point of the parabola
        focus_point = self.grid["D3"]
        focus_dot = Dot(focus_point, color=COLOR_RAY)
        focus_label = Text("Focus", font_size=14, color=COLOR_RAY)
        self.place_at_grid(focus_label, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        focus_label.next_to(focus_dot, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Incoming rays
        rays = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            start_pos = self.grid["A" + str(i)] + UP * 0.5
            # Simplified reflection logic: hit the dish height and go to focus
            # Dish is roughly at row E.
            hit_pos = np.array([start_pos[0], self.grid["E3"][1] - 0.2, 0])
            in_ray = Line(start_pos, hit_pos, color=COLOR_RAY, stroke_width=2)
            out_ray = Line(hit_pos, focus_point, color=COLOR_RAY, stroke_width=2)
            rays.add(VGroup(in_ray, out_ray))

        self.play(Create(dish))
        self.play(FadeIn(focus_dot), Write(focus_label))
        
        for ray_pair in rays:
            self.play(Create(ray_pair[0]), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(Create(ray_pair[1]), run_time=0.3)
        
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Pure geometry reveals the deep soul of conic sections.

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_SUMMARY)
        )

        summary_text = Text("Geometry and Algebra Unified", font_size=24, color=COLOR_SUMMARY)
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "A2", "A5")

        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.play(Indicate(summary_text, color=COLOR_SUMMARY))
        
        self.wait(3)

        self.setup_layout("The Mystery of the Slice", [
            "Conic sections are formed by slicing a double cone.",
            "We get ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas from different angles.",
            "How do these shapes connect to their algebraic definitions?"
        ])
        
        # Define Colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Create a double cone using polygons to represent its 2D projection
        # Upper cone triangle
        cone_upper = Polygon(
            [0, 0, 0], [1.5, 2, 0], [-1.5, 2, 0], 
            color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        )
        # Lower cone triangle
        cone_lower = Polygon(
            [0, 0, 0], [1.5, -2, 0], [-1.5, -2, 0], 
            color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        )

            [-1.5, -0.2, 0], [1.5, 0.8, 0], [1.8, 1.2, 0], [-1.2, 0.2, 0],
            color=PLANE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=2
        )
        # Place it such that it intersects the upper cone
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'C2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        plane.shift(UP * 0.5)

        # The intersection curve is an ellipse
        intersection_curve = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=0.3, color=CURVE_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        intersection_curve.rotate(15 * DEGREES)
        # Position it to align with the plane's intersection on the cone
        self.place_at_grid(intersection_curve, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        intersection_curve.shift(UP * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(plane, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(intersection_curve), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        section_label = Text("Conic Section", font_size=20, color=CURVE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(section_label, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Arrows to point to the objects
        # Point to lower cone for 'Cone' label
        arrow_cone = Arrow(
            cone_label.get_left(), 
            self.grid['C3'] + UP*0.5, # Pointing near the cone
            color=WHITE, buff=0.1, stroke_width=3
        )
        # Point to the intersection curve
        arrow_section = Arrow(
            section_label.get_left(), 
            intersection_curve.get_center(), 
            color=CURVE_COLOR, buff=0.2, stroke_width=3
        )

        self.play(
            Write(cone_label),
            Write(section_label),
            GrowArrow(arrow_cone),
            GrowArrow(arrow_section)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color for final view
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

            "Let's pick any point P on the ellipse's edge.",
            "We will track the distance from P to each focus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Foci", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_FOCI = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_P = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_GEN = "#FFFFFF"

        # Parameters

        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"]
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"]

        v_pos = (self.grid["A3"] + self.grid["A4"]) / 2 # Apex at A3.5
        vt1_dist = 1.2 # Constant distance from V to T1
        vt2_dist = 5.2 # Constant distance from V to T2 (vt1 + 2a)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FOCI)

            t = theta.get_value()
            return center + np.array([a * np.cos(t), b * np.sin(t), 0])
        
        p_dot = Dot(get_p_pos(), color=COLOR_P)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_p_pos()))
        
        p_label = Text("P", font_size=18, color=COLOR_P)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.05))

            norm = np.linalg.norm(vec)

            return v_pos + get_gen_unit_vec() * vt1_dist
            
        def get_t2_pos():
            return v_pos + get_gen_unit_vec() * vt2_dist

        gen_line = Line(v_pos, get_t2_pos(), color=COLOR_GEN, stroke_width=2)

I have completed the Manim code for **Section 4: Defining the Foci**.

### Key Implementation Details:
- **Visual Anchor System**: Used the 6x6 grid (`A1-F6`) for all element positioning. The ellipse is centered in the `D3.5` area, with foci at `D2` and `D5`.
- **Dynamic Animation**: Employed a `ValueTracker` for the position of point **P** on the ellipse. All associated elements—the segments $PF_1$ and $PF_2$, the generator line, and the tangency points $T_1$ and $T_2$—automatically update as **P** moves.
- **Dandelin's Proof Geometry**: Represented the generator line from vertex $V$ through $P$, identifying $T_1$ and $T_2$ such that $VT_1$ and $VT_2$ are constant, satisfying the geometric condition $PF_1 + PF_2 = VT_2 - VT_1$.
- **Style Consistency**: Followed the color constraints: Foci ($F_1, F_2$) in `#FFA500`, point $P$ in `#FF4500`, and the generator line/points in `#FFFFFF`.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # TEACHING CONTENT
        lecture_lines = [
            "The spheres' contact points on the plane are the foci.",
            "Let's pick any point P on the ellipse's edge.",
            "We will track the distance from P to each focus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Foci", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_FOCI = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_P = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_GEN = "#FFFFFF"

        # Parameters
        # Grid positions for layout
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"]
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"]
        center = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        a = 2.0
        c = 1.5
        b = np.sqrt(a**2 - c**2) # approx 1.32
        v_pos = (self.grid["A3"] + self.grid["A4"]) / 2 # Apex at A3.5
        vt1_dist = 1.2 # Constant distance from V to T1
        vt2_dist = 5.2 # Constant distance from V to T2 (vt1 + 2a)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: "The spheres' contact points on the plane are the foci."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_FOCI)
        
        # Draw the elliptical intersection
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=2*a, height=2*b, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).move_to(center)
        
        # Contact points F1 and F2
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=COLOR_FOCI)
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=COLOR_FOCI)
        f1_label = Text("F1", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FOCI).next_to(f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        f2_label = Text("F2", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FOCI).next_to(f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1, f2, f1_label, f2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: "Let's pick any point P on the ellipse's edge."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_P)
        
        # Use ValueTracker for the angle of point P on the ellipse
        theta = ValueTracker(60 * DEGREES)
        
        def get_p_pos():
            t = theta.get_value()
            return center + np.array([a * np.cos(t), b * np.sin(t), 0])
        
        p_dot = Dot(get_p_pos(), color=COLOR_P)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_p_pos()))
        
        p_label = Text("P", font_size=18, color=COLOR_P)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(p_dot, p_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: "We will track the distance from P to each focus."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_GEN)
        
        # 3. Draw segments from P to F1 and P to F2
        line_pf1 = Line(get_p_pos(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_FOCI, stroke_width=2)
        line_pf2 = Line(get_p_pos(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_FOCI, stroke_width=2)
        
        line_pf1.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(get_p_pos(), f1_pos))
        line_pf2.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(get_p_pos(), f2_pos))
        
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Trace a generator line from the cone's vertex through point P.
        v_dot = Dot(v_pos, color=COLOR_GEN, radius=0.06)
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GEN).next_to(v_dot, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        def get_gen_unit_vec():
            p = get_p_pos()
            vec = p - v_pos
            norm = np.linalg.norm(vec)
            return vec / norm if norm > 0 else RIGHT
            
        def get_t1_pos():
            return v_pos + get_gen_unit_vec() * vt1_dist
            
        def get_t2_pos():
            return v_pos + get_gen_unit_vec() * vt2_dist

        # The generator line goes from V to T2
        gen_line = Line(v_pos, get_t2_pos(), color=COLOR_GEN, stroke_width=2)
        gen_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(v_pos, get_t2_pos()))
        
        # 5. Identify points T1 and T2 where the generator line meets the contact circles.
        t1_dot = Dot(get_t1_pos(), color=COLOR_GEN)
        t2_dot = Dot(get_t2_pos(), color=COLOR_GEN)
        t1_label = Text("T1", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GEN)
        t2_label = Text("T2", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GEN)
        
        t1_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t1_pos()))
        t2_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t2_pos()))
        t1_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t1_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        t2_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t2_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(v_dot, v_label))
        self.play(Create(gen_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(t1_dot, t2_dot, t1_label, t2_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Movement to show relationship consistency across the ellipse
        # This highlights the proof step conceptually as P moves.
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(135 * DEGREES), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(-45 * DEGREES), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)
```

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Enter the Dandelin Spheres", [
            "Place two spheres inside the cone for an ellipse.",
            "Each sphere touches the cone along a perfect circle.",
            "The spheres also touch the cutting plane at one point.",
            "Germinal Dandelin introduced these 'kissing spheres' in 1822.",
            "These spheres reveal the hidden geometry of the conic slice."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_CONE = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_PLANE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_SPHERE_UP = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_SPHERE_DOWN = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_CONTACT = "#ADFF2F"
        COLOR_FOCAL = "#FFA500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SPHERE_UP)
        
        # Cone Setup (2D projection)
        y_apex = 2.5
        cone_lines = VGroup(
            Line(UP * y_apex, LEFT * 2.5 + DOWN * 2.5, color=COLOR_CONE),
            Line(UP * y_apex, RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 2.5, color=COLOR_CONE)
        )
        # Cutting plane
        plane_line = Line(LEFT * 2 + UP * 0.0, RIGHT * 2 + UP * 2.0, color=COLOR_PLANE)
        
        # Spheres
        sphere_up = Circle(radius=0.48, color=COLOR_SPHERE_UP, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(UP * 1.54)
        sphere_down = Circle(radius=1.70, color=COLOR_SPHERE_DOWN, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(UP * (-0.9))
        
        geom_group = VGroup(cone_lines, plane_line, sphere_up, sphere_down)
        self.place_in_area(geom_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(cone_lines))
        self.play(Create(plane_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_up), FadeIn(sphere_down))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CONTACT)
        
        # Calculate contact line positions based on current sphere positions
        # The scale of geom_group was 0.7, so we use current coordinates.
        y_c1 = sphere_up.get_center()[1]
        y_c2 = sphere_down.get_center()[1]
        # Relative contact offsets (scaled)
        # 1.5 * r * scale_factor
        off1 = (1.5 * 0.48 - 2.5 + 1.54) * 0.7 # No, let's just use the visual height
        # Simplified horizontal lines at the tangency points
        # For cone half-angle 30 deg, tangency is at y_c + r*sin(30)
        # But we need to account for the apex position.
        # Let's just place them relative to the centers.
        
        c_line1 = Line(
            sphere_up.get_center() + UP * (0.24 * 0.7) + LEFT * (0.42 * 0.7),
            sphere_up.get_center() + UP * (0.24 * 0.7) + RIGHT * (0.42 * 0.7),
            color=COLOR_CONTACT, stroke_width=4
        )
        c_line2 = Line(
            sphere_down.get_center() + UP * (0.85 * 0.7) + LEFT * (1.47 * 0.7),
            sphere_down.get_center() + UP * (0.85 * 0.7) + RIGHT * (1.47 * 0.7),
            color=COLOR_CONTACT, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(c_line1), Create(c_line2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_FOCAL)
        
        fp1_pos = plane_line.get_projection(sphere_up.get_center())
        fp2_pos = plane_line.get_projection(sphere_down.get_center())
        
        dot1 = Dot(fp1_pos, color=COLOR_FOCAL, radius=0.08)
        dot2 = Dot(fp2_pos, color=COLOR_FOCAL, radius=0.08)
        
        lbl1 = Text("F1", font_size=16, color=COLOR_FOCAL).next_to(dot1, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        lbl2 = Text("F2", font_size=16, color=COLOR_FOCAL).next_to(dot2, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2))
        self.play(Write(lbl1), Write(lbl2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        hist = Text("Germinal Dandelin (1822)", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(hist, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(hist))
        self.play(Indicate(sphere_up), Indicate(sphere_down))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        p_on_p = plane_line.point_from_proportion(0.3)
        dot_p = Dot(p_on_p, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        conn1 = Line(dot1.get_center(), p_on_p, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        conn2 = Line(dot2.get_center(), p_on_p, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_p))
        self.play(Create(conn1), Create(conn2))
        self.play(Indicate(conn1), Indicate(conn2))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof (The String Property)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Segment PF1 equals the distance to the top circle.",
            "Segment PF2 equals the distance to the bottom circle.",
            "Both distances lie along the same line on the cone.",
            "Their sum is the fixed distance between the two circles.",
            "This sum remains constant, proving it is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Base Geometry Construction ===
        # Geometry is defined in a local space and then placed in the grid area.
        v_pt_local = np.array([0, 2.8, 0])
        cone_l_local = Line(v_pt_local, [-2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        cone_r_local = Line(v_pt_local, [2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        
        s1_center_local = np.array([0, 1.2, 0])
        s1_radius = 0.7
        s1_local = Circle(radius=s1_radius, color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=3).move_to(s1_center_local)
        
        s2_center_local = np.array([0, -1.0, 0])
        s2_radius = 1.4
        s2_local = Circle(radius=s2_radius, color=BLUE_D, stroke_width=3).move_to(s2_center_local)
        
        # Tangency angle for the ellipse cross-section line
        angle = 20 * DEGREES
        f1_pt_local = s1_center_local + s1_radius * np.array([np.sin(angle), -np.cos(angle), 0])
        f2_pt_local = s2_center_local + s2_radius * np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
        ellipse_line_local = Line(f1_pt_local + 1.2*LEFT, f2_pt_local + 1.2*RIGHT, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Foci dots and labels
        f1_local = Dot(f1_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f2_local = Dot(f2_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f1_label_local = MathTex("F_1", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f1_local, UR, buff=0.05)
        f2_label_local = MathTex("F_2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f2_local, DL, buff=0.05)
        
        # Contact lines where spheres touch the cone surface (2D representation)
        y_c1_local = 1.2 - 0.7 * 0.42 
        y_c2_local = -1.0 - 1.4 * 0.42
        c_line1_local = Line([-0.8, y_c1_local, 0], [0.8, y_c1_local, 0], color=BLUE_A, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        c_line2_local = Line([-1.8, y_c2_local, 0], [1.8, y_c2_local, 0], color=BLUE_C, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)

            cone_l_local, cone_r_local, s1_local, s2_local, 
            ellipse_line_local, f1_local, f2_local, 
            f1_label_local, f2_label_local, c_line1_local, c_line2_local
        )
        self.place_in_area(diagram, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Scene coordinate references for updaters
        v_scene = cone_l_local.get_start()
        f1_scene = f1_local.get_center()
        f2_scene = f2_local.get_center()
        y_c1_scene = c_line1_local.get_center()[1]
        y_c2_scene = c_line2_local.get_center()[1]

        # === Dynamic Animation Setup ===
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.2)
        
        def get_p_pos():
            return ellipse_line_local.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value())

        p_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_p_pos()))
        p_label = MathTex("P", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        def get_t_pos(y_target):
            v = v_scene
            p = get_p_pos()
            if abs(p[1] - v[1]) < 0.001: return v
            t = (y_target - v[1]) / (p[1] - v[1])
            return v + t * (p - v)

        t1_dot = Dot(color=BLUE_A, radius=0.05)

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof (The String Property)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Segment PF1 equals the distance to the top circle.",
            "Segment PF2 equals the distance to the bottom circle.",
            "Both distances lie along the same line on the cone.",
            "Their sum is the fixed distance between the two circles.",
            "This sum remains constant, proving it is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Base Geometry Construction ===
        # Geometry is defined in a local space and then placed in the grid area.
        v_pt_local = np.array([0, 2.8, 0])
        cone_l_local = Line(v_pt_local, [-2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        cone_r_local = Line(v_pt_local, [2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        
        s1_center_local = np.array([0, 1.2, 0])
        s1_radius = 0.7
        s1_local = Circle(radius=s1_radius, color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=3).move_to(s1_center_local)
        
        s2_center_local = np.array([0, -1.0, 0])
        s2_radius = 1.4
        s2_local = Circle(radius=s2_radius, color=BLUE_D, stroke_width=3).move_to(s2_center_local)
        
        # Tangency angle for the ellipse cross-section line
        angle = 20 * DEGREES
        f1_pt_local = s1_center_local + s1_radius * np.array([np.sin(angle), -np.cos(angle), 0])
        f2_pt_local = s2_center_local + s2_radius * np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
        ellipse_line_local = Line(f1_pt_local + 1.2*LEFT, f2_pt_local + 1.2*RIGHT, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Foci dots and labels
        f1_local = Dot(f1_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f2_local = Dot(f2_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f1_label_local = MathTex("F_1", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f1_local, UR, buff=0.05)
        f2_label_local = MathTex("F_2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f2_local, DL, buff=0.05)
        
        # Contact lines where spheres touch the cone surface (2D representation)
        y_c1_local = 1.2 - 0.7 * 0.42 
        y_c2_local = -1.0 - 1.4 * 0.42
        c_line1_local = Line([-0.8, y_c1_local, 0], [0.8, y_c1_local, 0], color=BLUE_A, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        c_line2_local = Line([-1.8, y_c2_local, 0], [1.8, y_c2_local, 0], color=BLUE_C, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)

        diagram = VGroup(
            cone_l_local, cone_r_local, s1_local, s2_local, 
            ellipse_line_local, f1_local, f2_local, 
            f1_label_local, f2_label_local, c_line1_local, c_line2_local
        )
        self.place_in_area(diagram, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Scene coordinate references for updaters
        v_scene = cone_l_local.get_start()
        f1_scene = f1_local.get_center()
        f2_scene = f2_local.get_center()
        y_c1_scene = c_line1_local.get_center()[1]
        y_c2_scene = c_line2_local.get_center()[1]

        # === Dynamic Animation Setup ===
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.2)
        
        def get_p_pos():
            return ellipse_line_local.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value())

        p_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_p_pos()))
        p_label = MathTex("P", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        # Function to find intersection of generator line (VP) with horizontal contact lines
        def get_t_pos(y_target):
            v = v_scene
            p = get_p_pos()
            if abs(p[1] - v[1]) < 0.001: return v
            t = (y_target - v[1]) / (p[1] - v[1])
            return v + t * (p - v)

        t1_dot = Dot(color=BLUE_A, radius=0.05)
        t1_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t_pos(y_c1_scene)))
        t2_dot = Dot(color=BLUE_C, radius=0.05)
        t2_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t_pos(y_c2_scene)))
        
        t1_label = MathTex("T_1", font_size=18, color=BLUE_A)
        t1_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t1_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.05))
        t2_label = MathTex("T_2", font_size=18, color=BLUE_C)
        t2_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t2_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.05))

        # Dynamic tangent segments
        pf1_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), f1_scene, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4))
        pt1_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), t1_dot.get_center(), color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4))
        
        pf2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), f2_scene, color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4))
        pt2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), t2_dot.get_center(), color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4))

        generator = always_redraw(lambda: Line(v_scene, get_p_pos(), color=GRAY_B, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.6))
        t1t2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(t1_dot.get_center(), t2_dot.get_center(), color="#FFD700", stroke_width=5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Segment PF1 equals the distance to the top circle.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF8C00")
        self.add(diagram, p_dot, p_label)
        self.play(Create(pf1_seg), Create(pt1_seg), FadeIn(t1_dot, t1_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Segment PF2 equals the distance to the bottom circle.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.play(Create(pf2_seg), Create(pt2_seg), FadeIn(t2_dot, t2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Both distances lie along the same line on the cone.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(generator))
        self.play(Create(t1t2_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Their sum is the fixed distance between the two circles.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        formula = MathTex("PF_1 + PF_2 = T_1T_2", font_size=28, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This sum remains constant, proving it is an ellipse.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Animate P moving along the ellipse cross-section
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        final_text = Text("PF1 + PF2 = Constant", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of conic sections (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) as slices of a cone. State the central challenge: How do we prove that a flat slice of a cone perfectly matches the algebraic definition of these curves?
section_1.example: Imagine a chef precisely slicing a solid chocolate cone with a flat knife. Depending on the angle, the rim of the chocolate slice changes shape. We need to find the 'focal points' of that chocolate slice.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem
section_2.content: Review the 'Tangent Segments Theorem': Two tangent segments to a sphere from the same external point are equal in length. This is the foundational logic for the Dandelin proof.
section_2.example: Visualize a basketball sitting in a hoop (a ring). Any point on that ring is the same distance to the point where the ball touches the ground if it were dropped vertically.

section_3.title: Enter the Dandelin Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce Germinal Dandelin's brilliant 1822 insight. For an elliptical slice, place two spheres inside the cone: one above the plane and one below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the cutting plane at exactly one point.
section_3.example: Imagine inflating two balloons inside a glass cone until they are wedged tight against the walls and just barely 'kiss' the slanted glass shelf (the cutting plane) passing through the middle.

section_4.title: Defining the Foci
section_4.content: Explain that the two points where the spheres touch the plane (F1 and F2) are exactly the foci of the ellipse. Pick an arbitrary point 'P' on the edge of the slice (the curve).
section_4.example: A tiny ant (Point P) walks along the edge of the cut. We are going to track the distance from the ant to the two 'kissing points' (F1 and F2) of the balloons.

section_5.title: The Visual Proof (The String Property)
section_5.content: Show that the distance PF1 equals the segment on the cone's surface from P to the top sphere's contact circle. Similarly for PF2 and the bottom sphere. Because these segments lie on the same 'generator line' of the cone, their sum (PF1 + PF2) is always equal to the fixed distance between the two circles of tangency.
section_5.example: Animate a string connecting F1 to the ant (P) and then to F2. As the ant moves, the string length remains constant, visually demonstrating the definition of an ellipse: PF1 + PF2 = Constant.

section_6.title: Universal Application
section_6.content: Briefly demonstrate that this logic isn't just for ellipses. By changing the angle of the plane, Dandelin spheres can also define the focus of a parabola or the two foci of a hyperbola.
section_6.example: Tilt the glass shelf steeply. One balloon moves to the other side of the cone's vertex. The 'sum' of distances becomes a 'difference,' perfectly matching the geometric definition of a hyperbola.

section_7.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
section_7.content: Summarize how Dandelin spheres bridge the gap between 3D solid geometry and 2D coordinate geometry. Mention how this explains planetary orbits and satellite dish designs.
section_7.example: Think of a satellite dish: its parabolic shape is designed so all 'rays' hit a single focus, just like the point where a single Dandelin sphere would touch that parabolic slice.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Mystery of the Slice", [
            "Conic sections are formed by slicing a double cone.",
            "We get ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas from different angles.",
            "How do these shapes connect to their algebraic definitions?"
        ])
        
        # Define Colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Create a double cone using polygons to represent its 2D projection
        # Upper cone triangle
        cone_upper = Polygon(
            [0, 0, 0], [1.5, 2, 0], [-1.5, 2, 0], 
            color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        )
        # Lower cone triangle
        cone_lower = Polygon(
            [0, 0, 0], [1.5, -2, 0], [-1.5, -2, 0], 
            color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        )
        double_cone = VGroup(cone_upper, cone_lower)
        self.place_in_area(double_cone, 'B2', 'E4', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(double_cone), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Define a slicing plane (represented as a slanted surface)
        plane = Polygon(
            [-1.5, -0.2, 0], [1.5, 0.8, 0], [1.8, 1.2, 0], [-1.2, 0.2, 0],
            color=PLANE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=2
        )
        # Place it such that it intersects the upper cone
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'C2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        plane.shift(UP * 0.5)

        # The intersection curve is an ellipse
        intersection_curve = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=0.3, color=CURVE_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        intersection_curve.rotate(15 * DEGREES)
        # Position it to align with the plane's intersection on the cone
        self.place_at_grid(intersection_curve, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        intersection_curve.shift(UP * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(plane, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(intersection_curve), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Add labels for 'Cone' and 'Conic Section'
        cone_label = Text("Cone", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(cone_label, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        section_label = Text("Conic Section", font_size=20, color=CURVE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(section_label, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Arrows to point to the objects
        # Point to lower cone for 'Cone' label
        arrow_cone = Arrow(
            cone_label.get_left(), 
            self.grid['C3'] + UP*0.5, # Pointing near the cone
            color=WHITE, buff=0.1, stroke_width=3
        )
        # Point to the intersection curve
        arrow_section = Arrow(
            section_label.get_left(), 
            intersection_curve.get_center(), 
            color=CURVE_COLOR, buff=0.2, stroke_width=3
        )

        self.play(
            Write(cone_label),
            Write(section_label),
            GrowArrow(arrow_cone),
            GrowArrow(arrow_section)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Theorem"
        lines = [
            "Imagine two lines tangent to a sphere from one point.",
            "These two tangent segments are always equal in length.",
            "This simple geometric fact is our most powerful tool."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a sphere (#FFFFFF) and a point P (#FF4500) outside of it.
        # Sphere represented as a Circle with an Ellipse inside to give 3D depth
        sphere_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        sphere_ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=1.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=1).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        sphere = VGroup(sphere_circle, sphere_ellipse)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        point_p = Dot(color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(point_p, 'C1')
        label_p = MathTex("P", color="#FF4500", font_size=24).next_to(point_p, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw two tangent segments from P to points A and B (#00FF00) on the sphere's surface.
        # We'll calculate tangent points on the circle.
        # Circle center is at self.grid['B2'] to 'E5' center.
        circle_center = sphere.get_center()
        radius = 1.5
        p_pos = point_p.get_center()
        
        # Geometry for tangent points from P to Circle
        # Distance from center to P
        dist = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - circle_center)
        # Angle from center to P
        angle_p = np.arctan2(p_pos[1] - circle_center[1], p_pos[0] - circle_center[0])
        # Angle of tangent points relative to center-P line
        # cos(alpha) = radius / dist
        alpha = np.arccos(radius / dist)
        
        pos_a = circle_center + np.array([
            radius * np.cos(angle_p + alpha),
            radius * np.sin(angle_p + alpha),
            0
        ])
        pos_b = circle_center + np.array([
            radius * np.cos(angle_p - alpha),
            radius * np.sin(angle_p - alpha),
            0
        ])
        
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color="#00FF00")
        dot_b = Dot(pos_b, color="#00FF00")
        label_a = MathTex("A", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(dot_b, DOWN + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color="#00FF00")
        line_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color="#00FF00")
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(line_pa), 
            Create(line_pb), 
            FadeIn(dot_a), 
            FadeIn(dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight segments PA and PB, and display the equation 'PA = PB' to show equality.
        equation = MathTex("PA = PB", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'A4')
        
        # Highlight: briefly pulse the lines
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            line_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            line_pb.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            Write(equation)
        )
        self.play(
            line_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=2),
            line_pb.animate.set_stroke(width=2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout("Enter the Dandelin Spheres", [
            "Place two spheres inside the cone for an ellipse.",
            "Each sphere touches the cone along a perfect circle.",
            "The spheres also touch the cutting plane at one point.",
            "Germinal Dandelin introduced these 'kissing spheres' in 1822.",
            "These spheres reveal the hidden geometry of the conic slice."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_CONE = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_PLANE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_SPHERE_UP = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_SPHERE_DOWN = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_CONTACT = "#ADFF2F"
        COLOR_FOCAL = "#FFA500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SPHERE_UP)
        
        # Cone Setup (2D projection)
        y_apex = 2.5
        cone_lines = VGroup(
            Line(UP * y_apex, LEFT * 2.5 + DOWN * 2.5, color=COLOR_CONE),
            Line(UP * y_apex, RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 2.5, color=COLOR_CONE)
        )
        # Cutting plane
        plane_line = Line(LEFT * 2 + UP * 0.0, RIGHT * 2 + UP * 2.0, color=COLOR_PLANE)
        
        # Spheres
        sphere_up = Circle(radius=0.48, color=COLOR_SPHERE_UP, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(UP * 1.54)
        sphere_down = Circle(radius=1.70, color=COLOR_SPHERE_DOWN, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(UP * (-0.9))
        
        geom_group = VGroup(cone_lines, plane_line, sphere_up, sphere_down)
        self.place_in_area(geom_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(cone_lines))
        self.play(Create(plane_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_up), FadeIn(sphere_down))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CONTACT)
        
        # Calculate contact line positions based on current sphere positions
        # The scale of geom_group was 0.7, so we use current coordinates.
        y_c1 = sphere_up.get_center()[1]
        y_c2 = sphere_down.get_center()[1]
        # Relative contact offsets (scaled)
        # 1.5 * r * scale_factor
        off1 = (1.5 * 0.48 - 2.5 + 1.54) * 0.7 # No, let's just use the visual height
        # Simplified horizontal lines at the tangency points
        # For cone half-angle 30 deg, tangency is at y_c + r*sin(30)
        # But we need to account for the apex position.
        # Let's just place them relative to the centers.
        
        c_line1 = Line(
            sphere_up.get_center() + UP * (0.24 * 0.7) + LEFT * (0.42 * 0.7),

        )

            sphere_down.get_center() + UP * (0.85 * 0.7) + RIGHT * (1.47 * 0.7),
            color=COLOR_CONTACT, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(c_line1), Create(c_line2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_FOCAL)
        
        fp1_pos = plane_line.get_projection(sphere_up.get_center())
        fp2_pos = plane_line.get_projection(sphere_down.get_center())
        
        dot1 = Dot(fp1_pos, color=COLOR_FOCAL, radius=0.08)
        dot2 = Dot(fp2_pos, color=COLOR_FOCAL, radius=0.08)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        hist = Text("Germinal Dandelin (1822)", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)

        self.play(Write(hist))

        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(p_dot, p_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: "We will track the distance from P to each focus."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_GEN)
        
        # 3. Draw segments from P to F1 and P to F2
        line_pf1 = Line(get_p_pos(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_FOCI, stroke_width=2)

        line_pf2.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(get_p_pos(), f2_pos))

            p = get_p_pos()
            vec = p - v_pos
            norm = np.linalg.norm(vec)
            return vec / norm if norm > 0 else RIGHT
            
        def get_t1_pos():
            return v_pos + get_gen_unit_vec() * vt1_dist

        self.play(FadeIn(v_dot, v_label))
        self.play(Create(gen_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(t1_dot, t2_dot, t1_label, t2_label))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof (The String Property)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Segment PF1 equals the distance to the top circle.",
            "Segment PF2 equals the distance to the bottom circle.",
            "Both distances lie along the same line on the cone.",
            "Their sum is the fixed distance between the two circles.",
            "This sum remains constant, proving it is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Base Geometry Construction ===
        # Geometry is defined in a local space and then placed in the grid area.
        v_pt_local = np.array([0, 2.8, 0])
        cone_l_local = Line(v_pt_local, [-2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        cone_r_local = Line(v_pt_local, [2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        
        s1_center_local = np.array([0, 1.2, 0])
        s1_radius = 0.7
        s1_local = Circle(radius=s1_radius, color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=3).move_to(s1_center_local)
        
        s2_center_local = np.array([0, -1.0, 0])
        s2_radius = 1.4
        s2_local = Circle(radius=s2_radius, color=BLUE_D, stroke_width=3).move_to(s2_center_local)
        
        # Tangency angle for the ellipse cross-section line
        angle = 20 * DEGREES
        f1_pt_local = s1_center_local + s1_radius * np.array([np.sin(angle), -np.cos(angle), 0])
        f2_pt_local = s2_center_local + s2_radius * np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
        ellipse_line_local = Line(f1_pt_local + 1.2*LEFT, f2_pt_local + 1.2*RIGHT, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Foci dots and labels
        f1_local = Dot(f1_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f2_local = Dot(f2_pt_local, color=YELLOW, radius=0.06)
        f1_label_local = MathTex("F_1", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f1_local, UR, buff=0.05)
        f2_label_local = MathTex("F_2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f2_local, DL, buff=0.05)
        
        # Contact lines where spheres touch the cone surface (2D representation)
        y_c1_local = 1.2 - 0.7 * 0.42 
        y_c2_local = -1.0 - 1.4 * 0.42
        c_line1_local = Line([-0.8, y_c1_local, 0], [0.8, y_c1_local, 0], color=BLUE_A, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        c_line2_local = Line([-1.8, y_c2_local, 0], [1.8, y_c2_local, 0], color=BLUE_C, stroke_width=1.5, stroke_opacity=0.4)

        diagram = VGroup(
            cone_l_local, cone_r_local, s1_local, s2_local, 
            ellipse_line_local, f1_local, f2_local, 
            f1_label_local, f2_label_local, c_line1_local, c_line2_local
        )
        self.place_in_area(diagram, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Scene coordinate references for updaters
        v_scene = cone_l_local.get_start()
        f1_scene = f1_local.get_center()
        f2_scene = f2_local.get_center()
        y_c1_scene = c_line1_local.get_center()[1]
        y_c2_scene = c_line2_local.get_center()[1]

        # === Dynamic Animation Setup ===
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.2)
        
        def get_p_pos():
            return ellipse_line_local.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value())

        p_dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_p_pos()))
        p_label = MathTex("P", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        # Function to find intersection of generator line (VP) with horizontal contact lines
        def get_t_pos(y_target):
            v = v_scene
            p = get_p_pos()
            if abs(p[1] - v[1]) < 0.001: return v
            t = (y_target - v[1]) / (p[1] - v[1])
            return v + t * (p - v)

        t1_dot = Dot(color=BLUE_A, radius=0.05)
        t1_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t_pos(y_c1_scene)))
        t2_dot = Dot(color=BLUE_C, radius=0.05)
        t2_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_t_pos(y_c2_scene)))
        
        t1_label = MathTex("T_1", font_size=18, color=BLUE_A)
        t1_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t1_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.05))
        t2_label = MathTex("T_2", font_size=18, color=BLUE_C)
        t2_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(t2_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.05))

        # Dynamic tangent segments
        pf1_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), f1_scene, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4))
        pt1_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), t1_dot.get_center(), color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4))
        
        pf2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), f2_scene, color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4))
        pt2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_p_pos(), t2_dot.get_center(), color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4))

        generator = always_redraw(lambda: Line(v_scene, get_p_pos(), color=GRAY_B, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.6))
        t1t2_seg = always_redraw(lambda: Line(t1_dot.get_center(), t2_dot.get_center(), color="#FFD700", stroke_width=5))

        # --- Animations ---

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF8C00")
        self.add(diagram, p_dot, p_label)
        self.play(Create(pf1_seg), Create(pt1_seg), FadeIn(t1_dot, t1_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.play(Create(pf2_seg), Create(pt2_seg), FadeIn(t2_dot, t2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(generator))
        self.play(Create(t1t2_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        formula = MathTex("PF_1 + PF_2 = T_1T_2", font_size=28, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Animate P moving along the ellipse cross-section
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        final_text = Text("PF1 + PF2 = Constant", font_size=24, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

        focus_label.next_to(focus_dot, UP, buff=0.1)

        rays = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            start_pos = self.grid["A" + str(i)] + UP * 0.5
            # Simplified reflection logic: hit the dish height and go to focus
            # Dish is roughly at row E.
            hit_pos = np.array([start_pos[0], self.grid["E3"][1] - 0.2, 0])
            in_ray = Line(start_pos, hit_pos, color=COLOR_RAY, stroke_width=2)
            out_ray = Line(hit_pos, focus_point, color=COLOR_RAY, stroke_width=2)
            rays.add(VGroup(in_ray, out_ray))

        self.play(Create(dish))
        self.play(FadeIn(focus_dot), Write(focus_label))
        
        for ray_pair in rays:
            self.play(Create(ray_pair[0]), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(Create(ray_pair[1]), run_time=0.3)
        
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Pure geometry reveals the deep soul of conic sections.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_SUMMARY)
        )

        summary_text = Text("Geometry and Algebra Unified", font_size=24, color=COLOR_SUMMARY)
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "A2", "A5")

        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.play(Indicate(summary_text, color=COLOR_SUMMARY))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.content: Show that the distance PF1 equals the segment on the cone's surface from P to the top sphere's contact circle. Similarly for PF2 and the bottom sphere. Because these segments lie on the same 'generator line' of the cone, their sum (PF1 + PF2) is always equal to the fixed distance between the two circles of tangency.
outline.example: Animate a string connecting F1 to the ant (P) and then to F2. As the ant moves, the string length remains constant, visually demonstrating the definition of an ellipse: PF1 + PF2 = Constant.
